author: rafaelroquetto
body:
This PR addresses a few issues with the IP options mechanism namely:

1. deal with IP headers already containing IP options, ensuring they are not corrupt and that options are iterated properly
3. fix a broken assumption that tc ingress == request ingress path (and likewise, tc egress == request egress path). This is not always true. In k8s for instance, we end up attaching to the host `veth` of a given service pod, which will see traffic leaving the POD as _ingress_ (`pod eth0 (egress) ----> (ingress) host veth`).
4. Add a unit test for the IP propagation case only - we skip the JSON RPC hop as it's loopback traffic that we cannot see (in the real world, that would be covered by blackbox CP, HTTP headers and TCP options).

author: abretonc7s
body:
## **Description**

Add USDH collateral support for HIP-3 DEXs on HyperLiquid.

Some HIP-3 DEXs (like `vntl`, `flx`) use USDH as collateral instead of USDC. This PR automatically detects USDH DEXs and acquires USDH collateral by transferring USDC to spot and swapping to USDH before placing orders.

HyperLiquid spot has a $10 minimum order value, so first-time USDH DEX trades require $10 USDC available.

## **Changelog**

CHANGELOG entry: Added support for trading on USDH-collateralized HIP-3 DEXs with automatic USDC→USDH conversion

## **Related issues**

Fixes:

## **Manual testing steps**

```gherkin
Feature: USDH DEX Trading

  Scenario: User places order on USDH DEX with sufficient balance
    Given user has $10+ USDC in main perps balance
    And user has 0 USDH in spot

    When user places a $10 order on vntl:SPACEX at 3x leverage
    Then order is placed successfully

  Scenario: User places order on USDH DEX with insufficient balance
    Given user has < $10 USDC available
    And user has 0 USDH in spot

    When user places a $10 order on vntl:SPACEX
    Then error message explains $10 minimum requirement
```

> [!NOTE]
> Adds automatic USDH collateral handling for HIP-3 DEXs by detecting USDH markets and acquiring USDH via USDC→USDH spot swaps before placing orders.
> 
> - **Perps/HyperLiquid**:
>   - **USDH Collateral Support**:
>     - Add `USDH_CONFIG` (token name, swap slippage bps) in `constants/hyperLiquidConfig.ts`.
>     - Detect USDH-collateralized DEXs via `isUsdhCollateralDex()` using `meta()` and `spotMeta()`.
>     - Retrieve spot balances (`getSpotUsdhBalance()`, `getSpotUsdcBalance()`), transfer USDC to spot (`transferUsdcToSpot()`), and swap USDC→USDH (`swapUsdcToUsdh()`) with slippage and $10 minimum order handling.
>     - Ensure USDH collateral before HIP-3 orders with `ensureUsdhCollateralForOrder()`; integrate into `handleHip3PreOrder()` so USDH DEXs pull from spot automatically.
>   - **Misc**: Additional logging/error handling and minor integrations around order flow without altering non-USDH paths.

body:
### 🔗 Related Issue
- https://github.com/jam2in/arcus-works/issues/784

### ⌨️ What I did
### first commit: 
- `process_command_ascii()`의 로직을 첫 문자 비교를 먼저 수행하게 변경했습니다.

### second commit:
- ntokens 검사를 `process_command_ascii()`에서 각 명령 처리 함수에 넘겼습니다.
    - cmdlog, lqdetect, shutdown 명령에 대해 ntokens 상한치를 설정했습니다.
- **ntokens 범위를 위배한 경우에 대한 에러 출력이 변경**되었습니다.
    - command가 올바르지 않은 경우 `ERROR unknown command` 출력, command는 올바르지만 ntokens가 허용 범위를 벗어난 경우 `CLIENT_ERROR bad command line format` 출력, command가 올바르고 ntokens가 허용 범위 내에 있지만 subcommand token이 올바르진 않은 경우 `ERROR unknown command` 출력하게 변경했습니다.
    - 다음은 일부 예시입니다.
    
command line | as is | to be
-- | -- | --
cmdlog | Usage: cmdlog [start [path] / stop / stats] | Usage: cmdlog [start [path] / stop / stats]
cmdlog abc | Usage: cmdlog [start [path] / stop / stats] | Usage: cmdlog [start [path] / stop / stats]
cmdlog stop abc def | command logging already stopped. | Usage: cmdlog [start [path] / stop / stats]
scan | ERROR unknown command | CLIENT_ERROR bad command line format
scan kyaa | ERROR unknown command | CLIENT_ERROR bad command line format
scan key | ERROR unknown command | CLIENT_ERROR bad command line format
scan abc def | ERROR unknown command | ERROR unknown command
bop | ERROR unknown command | CLIENT_ERROR bad command line format
bop eenzult | ERROR unknown command | CLIENT_ERROR bad command line format
bop insert | ERROR unknown command | CLIENT_ERROR bad command line format
bop eenzult kvkey 10 2 | ERROR unknown command | ERROR unknown command
bop insert kvkey 10 | ERROR unknown command | CLIENT_ERROR bad command line format
shutdown 3 abc | OK / DENIED | CLIENT_ERROR bad command line format

body:
…ttings menu

Major Features:
- Added inverse frequency mapping helpers (xToFrequency, getBinIndex)
- Refactored spectrum to high-resolution heatmap bar visualization with peak detection
- Enhanced spectrum with dual-layer visualization (Live fill + Average curve)
- Replaced oscilloscope with Rekordbox-style multi-colored frequency waveform
- Redesigned UI with floating settings menu to maximize screen space

Spectrum Visualization:
- Implemented pixel-perfect heatmap bar rendering with linear interpolation
- Each pixel column uses peak detection across frequency bins to preserve transients
- Added dual-layer rendering: Live gradient fill (smoothedData) + Average curve (averageData)
- Smoothing slider now controls average curve update rate (0.05-0.5 alpha)
- Live data uses fixed fast alpha (0.8) for responsive visualization

Chart Layout Improvements:
- Defined proper margin constants (MARGIN_LEFT=60, MARGIN_BOTTOM=30, MARGIN_TOP=20, MARGIN_RIGHT=20)
- Implemented canvas clipping to prevent data from overlapping axis labels
- Refactored drawDbMarkers and drawFrequencyMarkers to draw grid lines only in active area
- Labels positioned in margin areas, grid lines subtle with low opacity

Oscilloscope Redesign:
- Complete replacement with Rekordbox-style multi-colored waveform
- Added waveformColorBuffer parallel to waveformBuffer for frequency-based coloring
- Color calculation based on 3-band energy analysis:
  * Lows (20-250Hz) -> Red channel
  * Mids (250-2500Hz) -> Green channel
  * Highs (2500-20kHz) -> Blue channel
- Vertical line/rectangle rendering with per-pixel color mapping
- Waveform scrolls right-to-left showing frequency content at each moment

UI Redesign:
- Removed static controls section from main document flow
- Added floating settings button (gear icon) fixed bottom-right
- Created floating settings menu panel with backdrop blur
- All controls moved to floating menu (Audio Source, Play/Pause, Smoothing, Decay, View Length)
- Click-outside-to-close functionality for settings menu
- Maximized screen space for visualizations

Helper Functions:
- xToFrequency(x, width): Inverse logarithmic mapping from pixel to frequency
- getBinIndex(frequency, fftSize): Maps frequency to FFT bin index
- calculateFrequencyColor(fftData, fftSize): Calculates RGB color from frequency bands
- getBufferColor(index): Retrieves color from circular buffer with wrapping

Technical Improvements:
- Proper devicePixelRatio handling for HiDPI displays
- Canvas clipping for clean chart boundaries
- Maintained all existing control IDs for backward compatibility
- Optimized rendering with proper buffer management

body:
## Summary

Fixes TOML parsing to correctly handle dotted backend names like `grok-4.1-fast` and `deepseek.coder.v2` which are documented in the README but were not working due to how TOML parses dotted keys as nested dictionaries.

## Problem

When users define backends with dotted names in `llm_config.toml`:

```toml
[backends.grok-4.1-fast]
enabled = true
backend_type = "codex"
model = "x-ai/grok-4.1-fast:free"
```

TOML parsers convert this into nested dictionaries:

```python
{
  "grok-4": {
    "1-fast": {
      "enabled": true,
      "backend_type": "codex",
      ...
    }
  }
}
```

The previous implementation only looked for backends in the top-level `[backends]` section, causing these dotted-name backends to be silently ignored.

## Solution

Added recursive parsing logic to traverse nested dictionary structures and identify backend configurations:

1. **Extracted helper function**: `parse_backend_config()` for reusability
2. **Added heuristic detection**: `is_potential_backend_config()` identifies backend configs by checking for common backend fields
3. **Implemented recursive traversal**: `find_backends_recursive()` walks nested structures to find all backend definitions
4. **Preserved existing behavior**: Explicit `[backends]` section continues to work as before

## Changes

### `src/auto_coder/llm_backend_config.py`
- Refactored backend parsing to support both explicit `[backends]` section and top-level dotted keys
- Added recursive parsing with safeguards to avoid false positives
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing configurations

### `tests/test_llm_backend_config.py`
- Added comprehensive test for dotted keys (`grok-4.1-fast`)
- Added test for deeply nested backends (`deepseek.coder.v2`)
- Validates both single-level and multi-level nesting

## Testing

```python
# Test case 1: Single-level dotted key
[grok-4.1-fast]  # Parsed as {"grok-4": {"1-fast": {...}}}
# Result: Backend named "grok-4.1-fast" is correctly recognized

# Test case 2: Multi-level dotted key
[deepseek.coder.v2]  # Parsed as {"deepseek": {"coder": {"v2": {...}}}}
# Result: Backend named "deepseek.coder.v2" is correctly recognized
```

All existing tests pass, confirming backward compatibility.

## Impact

- ✅ Enables documented feature of using dotted backend names
- ✅ Maintains backward compatibility with existing configurations
- ✅ No breaking changes
- ✅ Comprehensive test coverage added

## Related Documentation

The README already documents this feature at line 332:
```toml
[backends.grok-4.1-fast]
enabled = true
backend_type = "codex"
```

This PR makes that documented example actually work.

…aths

The image proxy was returning 404 errors because the backend was prioritizing local thumbnail_file paths (e.g., /thumbs/78-coloretto.png) over BGG URLs. These local files don't exist on Render's ephemeral filesystem.

Changes:
- Reorder thumbnail URL priority in _game_to_dict() to check BGG image field first
- Fall back to BGG thumbnail_url field second
- Only use local thumbnail_file if it's not a /thumbs/ path
- Add comment explaining Render's ephemeral filesystem limitation

This ensures all game thumbnails use BGG URLs that can be properly proxied, eliminating the 502 Bad Gateway errors in production.

author: j-d-ha
body:
## 📋 Summary

This PR adds `ILambdaHostContextAccessor` interface and related context factory infrastructure to enable dependency injection of the current Lambda invocation context. The feature allows components throughout the application to access the `ILambdaHostContext` without requiring it to be passed as a method parameter.

**Key Changes:**
- New `ILambdaHostContextAccessor` interface in abstractions for context access
- `LambdaHostContextAccessor` implementation using `AsyncLocal<T>` for context storage
- `ILambdaHostContextFactory` interface and implementation for injected context creation
- Refactored `LambdaHandlerComposer` to use the context factory
- Extension method `AddLambdaHostContextAccessor()` for DI registration
- Comprehensive unit tests for new components
- Example project updates demonstrating usage

---

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] My changes build cleanly
- [x] I've added/updated relevant tests
- [x] I've added/updated documentation or README
- [x] I've followed the coding style for this project
- [x] I've tested the changes locally (if applicable)

---

## 🧪 Related Issues or PRs

Closes #177

---

## 💬 Notes for Reviewers

The accessor pattern follows the design from ASP.NET Core's `HttpContextAccessor` for consistency with the .NET ecosystem. The use of `AsyncLocal<T>` ensures context isolation across async execution flows, which is critical for Lambda's concurrent invocation model.

The `ILambdaHostContextAccessor` parameter in `LambdaHostContextFactory` is optional to maintain backwards compatibility and allow flexibility in DI configuration.

author: victoriashirleyunifei
body:
Esta pull request refatora os cards de animais e os componentes de modal para utilizarem dados reais de animais a partir de uma fonte mock, introduz gerenciamento de estado para o interesse do usuário em animais e melhora a navegação e a consistência da interface entre as páginas Home e Profile. As mudanças tornam a UI mais dinâmica e interativa, permitindo que usuários marquem interesse em animais e visualizem informações detalhadas.

**Cards e modais orientados a dados reais:**

* Refatorados os componentes `CardAnimal` e `ModalViewAnimal` para aceitarem uma prop `animal` e exibirem seus dados reais (nome, imagem, idade, sexo, porte, espécie, raça, descrição, status, comportamentos, informações do tutor, etc.), substituindo valores fixos.  

* Adicionada lógica para lidar com o toggle de interesse do usuário e com adoção de animais, atualizando a UI e o estado conforme necessário e repassando esses handlers como props para os componentes de card e modal.  
  
**Gerenciamento de estado e melhorias de renderização:**

* Atualizadas as páginas Home e Profile para utilizar `mockAnimals` como fonte de dados, manter o estado dos animais com React hooks e renderizar os cards dinamicamente com base no estado em vez de um número fixo.  
  
**Navegação e consistência da interface:**

* Melhorada a navegação do header, tornando o logo clicável e redirecionando para a Home.  

* Ajustado o comportamento do modal para redirecionar para a aba de interesses do perfil quando o usuário marca interesse em um animal, e para fechar o modal quando o animal é marcado como adotado.

Essas mudanças tornam o app mais interativo e mais fácil de manter, utilizando estruturas reais de dados e um gerenciamento de estado centralizado.

When the configmap hami-device-plugin has been custom modified, using helm upgrade will overwrite it with the default configuration of the template.

Add the devicePlugin.nodeConfiguration option, which includes 2 sub-items: config and configName:

1. Default value: The default value for both is empty, indicating the use of the default example configuration.

2. config: Specify a value for config.json (a JSON string) to override the default value.

3. externalConfigName: Specify an existing configmap to mount into the device-plugin (ensure the content is correct).

`zlib` 예제 프로그램에 **gzip 헤더의 FEXTRA(Extra field) 영역에 사용자 지정 메타데이터를 기록하는 기능** 추가

- 새 예제 파일: `test/minigzip_meta.c`
- 기능
  - gzip 헤더에 **작성자(Author)** 와 **날짜(Date)** 정보를 저장
  - Extra field 안에 다음과 같은 서브 필드를 사용
    - `AU` : Author 문자열
    - `DT` : Date 문자열

---

## 빌드 및 실행 방법

> 환경: 리눅스, zlib 소스가 `~/zlib` 에 클론되어 있다고 가정

### 1) zlib 빌드 (처음 한 번만)

```bash
cd ~/zlib
ls
# configure  Makefile.in  zlib.h  test/ ... 가 보이면 OK

./configure
make

ls libz.a
# libz.a  라고 보이면 빌드 완료
```

### 2) 예제 컴파일
```bash
cd ~/zlib/test
ls
# example.c, minigzip.c, minigzip_meta.c ... 가 있어야 함

gcc -I.. -o minigzip_meta minigzip_meta.c ../libz.a

ls minigzip_meta
# minigzip_meta* 처럼 보이고, 초록색(실행 파일)이면 OK
```

### 3) 입력 파일 만들기
```bash
echo "hello gzip meta test" > input.txt
ls
# input.txt  minigzip_meta ... 처럼 보이면 됨
```

### 4) 프로그램 실행
```bash
./minigzip_meta input.txt output.gz "C389033" "2025-11-24"
# 정상 실행 시:
# created output.gz with author='C389033', date='2025-11-24'
```
### 5) 결과 및 헤더 확인
```bash
ls
# input.txt  output.gz  minigzip_meta ... 처럼 output.gz 파일이 생성됨

gzip -dc output.gz
# 화면에 "hello gzip meta test" 가 출력되면 압축/해제는 정상 동작

hexdump -C output.gz | head
# 헤더 영역에서 'AU', 'DT' 와 함께 "C389033", "2025-11-24" 문자열이 들어간 것을 확인할 수 있음
```

## Summary

- Improve system resilience by transparently recovering from transient failures (connection timeouts, pool exhaustion, network errors)

## Changes

### Core Implementation
- **TransientSQLExceptionPredicate**: Classifies SQL exceptions by SQLSTATE prefix (08xxx=connection, 40xxx=deadlock, 53xxx=resources)
- **RetryEventLogger**: Structured logging with MDC context for retry observability
- **@Retry annotations**: Applied to all storage methods with configurable backoff

### Configuration
- 3 max retries with 200ms initial delay
- Exponential backoff with 5s max delay
- 30s max duration per operation

author: adryanev
body:
## Description
  This PR fixes memory leaks and improves React performance in the frontpage playlist
  components. Key changes include:

  - Adding `_isMounted` guards to prevent state updates after component unmount
  - Migrating from event listener patterns to React Context for layout state
  - Fixing useEffect cleanup and hook dependencies
  - Adding progressive loading for featured playlists
  - Limiting list items to 20 to prevent oversized DOM trees
  - Adding CSS containment to prevent layout shift during loading

  ## Related Issue
  Fixes #351 Closes #353 

  ## Motivation and Context
  The frontpage components were causing memory leaks due to:
  1. Missing cleanup of event listeners on component unmount
  2. State updates occurring after component unmount in async operations
  3. EventEmitter listeners accumulating without proper removal
  4. Unstable callback references causing listener recreation on every render

  These issues caused degraded performance over time and React warnings about "Can't
  perform a React state update on an unmounted component."

  ## How Has This Been Tested?
  - Manual testing of page navigation to verify no memory leak warnings
  - Verified featured playlists load progressively
  - Confirmed event listeners are properly cleaned up on unmount
  - Tested layout responsiveness with sidebar toggle

  ## Screenshots (if appropriate):
  N/A - Performance and memory improvements with no visual changes

  - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
  - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
  - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to

<issue_title>[feature/client] Windows Client for Managed Nebula</issue_title>
<issue_description>## User Story: Windows Client for Managed Nebula

**As a** Windows system administrator  
**I want** a native Windows client for Managed Nebula  
**So that** I can manage Nebula mesh VPN connections on Windows workstations and servers with the same ease as macOS clients

---

### Acceptance Criteria

#### 1. Core Functionality
- [ ] Client polls server API (`/api/v1/client/config`) every `POLL_INTERVAL_HOURS` (default 24h)
- [ ] Authenticates using client token stored securely in Windows registry or config file
- [ ] Generates Nebula keypair on first run using `nebula-cert keygen`
- [ ] Submits public key to server and receives configuration, certificate, and CA chain
- [ ] Writes Nebula config to `C:\ProgramData\Nebula\config.yml`
- [ ] Writes certificates to `C:\ProgramData\Nebula\host.crt` and `C:\ProgramData\Nebula\ca.crt`
- [ ] Writes private key to `C:\ProgramData\Nebula\host.key` with restricted permissions

#### 2. Service Integration
- [ ] Runs as a Windows Service using Python's `pywin32` or `nssm` wrapper
- [ ] Service starts automatically on system boot
- [ ] Service can be controlled via `sc.exe`, PowerShell, or Services MMC
- [ ] Service logs to Windows Event Log or file at `C:\ProgramData\Nebula\logs\agent.log`
- [ ] Graceful shutdown when service is stopped

#### 3. Nebula Binary Management
- [ ] Bundles Windows `nebula.exe` binary (or downloads on first run)
- [ ] Launches `nebula.exe` as subprocess with correct config path
- [ ] Monitors Nebula process health and restarts if crashed
- [ ] Captures Nebula stdout/stderr to log file

#### 4. Installation & Setup
- [ ] MSI or NSIS installer for easy deployment
- [ ] Installer registers Windows Service
- [ ] Installer prompts for initial client token or reads from config file
- [ ] Installer creates `C:\ProgramData\Nebula` directory with appropriate ACLs
- [ ] Uninstaller stops service, removes files, and cleans up registry

#### 5. Configuration Management
- [ ] Reads settings from `C:\ProgramData\Nebula\agent.ini` or registry
- [ ] Configurable server URL (default `http://localhost:8080`)
- [ ] Configurable poll interval (default 24 hours)
- [ ] Configurable log level (INFO, DEBUG, WARNING, ERROR)

#### 6. Security
- [ ] Private key file (`host.key`) restricted to SYSTEM and Administrators
- [ ] Client token stored with appropriate ACLs (not world-readable)
- [ ] Service runs as LocalSystem or dedicated service account
- [ ] HTTPS support with certificate validation

#### 7. Monitoring & Diagnostics
- [ ] Status command shows: service status, last poll time, current IP, Nebula version
- [ ] Logs all operations (config fetch, cert renewal, Nebula restarts)
- [ ] Exposes metrics for monitoring tools (optional)

---

### Technical Implementation Notes

1. **Project Structure**:
   ```
   client-windows/
   ├── agent.py              # Main agent logic (similar to macOS)
   ├── service.py            # Windows service wrapper
   ├── installer/            # MSI/NSIS installer scripts
   ├── requirements.txt      # Python dependencies
   └── README.md             # Windows-specific docs
   ```

2. **Key Dependencies**:
   - `pywin32` for Windows Service integration
   - `requests` for HTTP client
   - `pyyaml` for config generation
   - `pyinstaller` or `cx_Freeze` for standalone executable

3. **Service Registration**:
   ```powershell
   # Using sc.exe
   sc create NebulaAgent binPath="C:\Program Files\Nebula\agent.exe" start=auto
   
   # Or using nssm
   nssm install NebulaAgent "C:\Program Files\Nebula\agent.exe"
   ```

4. **File Paths** (Windows):
   - Config: `C:\ProgramData\Nebula\config.yml`
   - Certs: `C:\ProgramData\Nebula\host.crt`, `C:\ProgramData\Nebula\ca.crt`
   - Key: `C:\ProgramData\Nebula\host.key`
   - Agent config: `C:\ProgramData\Nebula\agent.ini`
   - Logs: `C:\ProgramData\Nebula\logs\agent.log`

5. **Registry Keys** (optional token storage):
   ```
   HKLM\SOFTWARE\ManagedNebula\ClientToken
   HKLM\SOFTWARE\ManagedNebula\ServerURL
   ```

---

### Out of Scope (Future Enhancements)

- GUI tray application for status monitoring
- Built-in firewall rule configuration
- Integration with Windows Defender
- Group Policy deployment templates
- PowerShell cmdlets for administration

The previous implementation compared `kcb->task_current` with the task’s list node in the global task list. A list node is only a linkage element, not a stable identifier for a task, so this comparison is not appropriate.

This patch updates the check to compare the task's data structure (TCB), which properly represents the task identity.

- label→mask 후 마스킹 복사 시 원본과 다른 형태
- 잔재만 남은 마스킹이 복사됨

원인:

  2. 이미지 파일에 전체 마스킹 저장 ✓
  3. draw_image() 호출
  4. 하지만 self.ci == self.pi이므로 즉시 리턴 ✗
  5. self.masking이 업데이트되지 않음 (여전히 bbox만)
- copy_masking_to_range()에서:
  1. target_img_array[self.masking] = [255, 0, 255]
  2. self.masking = bbox 픽셀만 → 잔재만 복사 ✗

body:
## Summary

Add Sucrose-inspired static analysis at executor creation time with bridge optimization. This enables:

- **Fail-fast validation** - Detect issues at `provide()`/`derive()` call time, not runtime
- **Better error context** - Capture call site where executor was defined for debugging
- **Foundation for devtools** - Analysis metadata enables future dependency graph visualization
- **Optimized execution** - Skip unused infrastructure (controller, dependency resolution)

### Key Insight

`new Function()` cannot access closures or imports - it runs in a fresh global scope. Since most real-world factories use imported classes, 90%+ of executors would skip compilation anyway.

**Solution:** Keep the original factory function, optimize the **bridge** between scope infrastructure and user's closure:
- Dependency resolution based on shape (none/single/array/record)
- Controller creation based on inference (NOOP_CONTROLLER or real)
- Optimized argument passing (skip unused params)
- Error enrichment for both sync and async errors

### Changes

- Add `sucrose.ts` with static analysis and bridge optimization
- Export `Sucrose` namespace, `analyze`, `compile`, `getMetadata` functions
- Integrate compilation into `createExecutor()` with graceful fallback
- Add `callSite` property to error classes for debugging
- Update scope.ts executeFactory with inference-based optimized calls
- Add comprehensive tests (200 total)

### ADR

See [ADR-002](https://github.com/pumped-fn/pumped-fn/blob/feat/sucrose-static-analysis/.c3/adr/adr-002-static-analysis-code-generation.md) for design decisions.

### Analysis Detects

| Property | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `usesCleanup` | Calls `ctl.cleanup()`? |
| `usesRelease` | Calls `ctl.release()`? |
| `usesReload` | Calls `ctl.reload()`? |
| `usesScope` | Accesses `ctl.scope`? |
| `dependencyShape` | `'single'` / `'array'` / `'record'` / `'none'` |
| `dependencyAccess` | Which dependencies are actually accessed |

### Bridge Optimization

Based on inference, optimize the execution path:

```typescript
// provide(() => 42)
// Inference: dependencyShape=none, usesController=false
// Optimized call: originalFactory() - no args needed

// derive([db], ([db]) => new Repository(db))
// Inference: dependencyShape=array, usesController=false
// Optimized call: originalFactory([resolvedDb]) - no controller

// provide((ctl) => { ctl.cleanup(...); return new Connection() })
// Inference: dependencyShape=none, usesCleanup=true
// Optimized call: originalFactory(controller) - controller needed
```

### Architecture

```
scope.resolve(executor)
       │
       ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Scope Layer                                                │
│  • Check value cache                                        │
│  • Apply preset substitutions                               │
│  • Extension wrap/onError                                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       │
       ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Inference-based Optimized Call                             │
│  • Resolve dependencies (based on shape or skip)            │
│  • Create controller (NOOP or real based on inference)      │
│  • Call originalFn with optimized args                      │
│  • Error enrichment (callSite, name)                        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       │
       ▼
originalFn(deps?, ctl?) ← user's closure, untouched
```

## Test plan

- [x] All 200 tests pass
- [x] Typecheck passes
- [x] Analysis correctly detects ctl methods, dependency access
- [x] Optimized calls work for all dependency shapes (none, single, array, record)
- [x] Call site captured at creation time
- [x] Error enrichment includes callSite
- [x] Controller only created when needed
- [x] Closures work correctly (original factory preserved)
- [x] Backward compatible - existing tests unchanged

body:
Resolves #25

### Setup

1. `vizier init`
1. (optional) `vizier deploy`
1. `vizier domain-setup` prompts for a domain, instructs the user on a DNS record to create, and confirms that the user created it
1. `vizier deploy` again updates the stack with the certificate, and instructs the user to create a second DNS record, actually directing traffic to their app

### Removal

- `vizier domain-remove` deletes the domain configuration, redeploys the stack with the change, and then deletes the certificate. (The certificate cannot be deleted while the stack is still using it.) This should work in the happy case, but could possibly be made more reliable.

OR

- `vizier destroy` deletes the domain configuration and certificate after deleting the stack

### Limitations

- when a domain has been set up, every redeploy triggers instructions to set up the second DNS record, regardless of whether they have already done it. We don't expect our users to redeploy from the CLI often, so maybe this is fine

### Next Steps

Testing:

- So far I have only tested with the static site variation, but they should all work the same.
- I have not tested GitHub redeployment with a custom domain enabled, but I don't think they should interact with each other at all so it should work fine.

Potential Enhancements:

- inform the user that their domain needs to be a fully qualified domain, not an apex domain (e.g. `www.vizier.xyz` is ok but not `vizier.xyz`)
- Make domainRemove action more robust. Currently it nukes the domain configuration file and then recreates it if deletion failed. Seems sketchy.

### Other Notes

- Extracted cloudfront distribution props to more easily facilitate conditional properties. This is more about code organization to appease typescript
- Extracted deploy stack action to a separate function that can be called independent of the command line. I did this because removing the custom domain requires redeploying the stack before deleting the certificate, so the domain removal command needed to be able to trigger a stack deployment.

body:
## Summary
Fixes the Prisma 7 compatibility error reported by collaborators where the `url` property in the datasource block is no longer supported.

## Problem
Collaborators encountered this error:
```
error: The datasource property `url` is no longer supported in schema files. 
Move connection URLs for Migrate to `prisma.config.ts` and pass either 
`adapter` for a direct database connection or `accelerateUrl` for Accelerate 
to the PrismaClient constructor.
```

## Solution
Removed the deprecated `url` property from `schema.prisma` since we're using the adapter pattern with `@prisma/adapter-pg`.

## Changes

### 🔧 Schema Fix
- **Removed**: `url = env("DATABASE_URL")` from `prisma/schema.prisma`
- **Why**: In Prisma 7, when using database adapters, the connection string is passed directly to the adapter (not in the schema)

### 🎯 ESLint Configuration
- **Added**: `app/generated/**` to ESLint global ignores
- **Why**: Prevents linting errors on Prisma-generated code that could halt Next.js dev server

## How It Works Now

The database connection is properly configured in `lib/prisma.ts`:

```typescript
const pool = new Pool({
  connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL,  // ← URL configured here
});
const adapter = new PrismaPg(pool);
const prisma = new PrismaClient({ adapter });  // ← Adapter pattern (Prisma 7 standard)
```

This is the correct pattern for Prisma 7 when using database adapters.

## Generator Configuration ✅

Our current generator output path is **correct** and follows Prisma 7 best practices:

```prisma
generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
  output   = "../app/generated/prisma"
}
```

### Why This is Right:
- ✅ Prisma 7 requires custom output paths (no longer generates in `node_modules`)
- ✅ `app/generated/prisma` is [Prisma's recommended path for Next.js](https://www.prisma.io/docs/guides/nextjs)
- ✅ Already excluded from `.gitignore`
- ✅ Now excluded from ESLint

## Testing
- ✅ `npx prisma generate` works without errors
- ✅ `npm run build` successful
- ✅ All TypeScript checks pass
- ✅ No linting errors

## Impact
- ✅ Resolves blocker for collaborators running `npx prisma generate`
- ✅ Fully compatible with Prisma 7
- ✅ No breaking changes for existing code

## References
- [Prisma 7 Generating Client Documentation](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-client/setup-and-configuration/generating-prisma-client)

Potential fix for [https://github.com/Adalk033/Alfred/security/code-scanning/5](https://github.com/Adalk033/Alfred/security/code-scanning/5)

The recommended fix is to avoid exposing raw exception information (`str(e)`) to external users in the HTTP API. Instead, log the detailed error (as is already done), but return a generic message in the API response and error list (`errors`). 

To do this:
- On line 3182, replace the construction of `error_msg` with a generic message that does not leak details of the exception (e.g., `"Se produjo un error procesando la ruta"`).
- Optionally, append a display-friendly descriptor including the path or index if needed for user context, avoiding the use of `str(e)` entirely.
- Ensure the error log uses the full exception (as presently), so developers/admins have complete debugging information.

>   - **Input**: `PlayerInputHandler` adds pickup/inventory keys and idle-on-release; jump/attack state handling refined.
>   - **Networking/Parsing**: `NetworkHandler` sends `characterType`; `GameStateParser` now parses `npcs`, `items`, `inventory`, `mesos`, `state`, `characterType`.

author: lawyzheng
body:
> [!IMPORTANT] > Adds a feature to automatically close oldest browser pages when the number of open pages exceeds a configurable limit, with a default of 10 pages. > > - **Behavior**: > - Adds `BROWSER_MAX_PAGES_NUMBER` setting in `skyvern/config.py` to limit open browser pages (default: 10). > - Modifies `list_valid_pages()` in `browser_factory.py` to close oldest pages when limit is exceeded, logging a warning. > - **Misc**: > - Updates initialization process for test notebooks. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=Skyvern-AI%2Fskyvern&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 13be71153222b0285d063ea2aee9022acbf07edf. You can [customize](https://app.ellipsis.dev/Skyvern-AI/settings/summaries) this summary. It will automatically update as commits are pushed. ---- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Browser now supports configurable page management with a default maximum of 10 pages. Older pages are automatically closed when the limit is exceeded. ✏️ Tip: You can customize this high-level summary in your review settings. --- 🔒 This PR implements automatic browser page management by introducing a configurable limit on the number of open pages and automatically closing the oldest pages when the limit is exceeded. The feature adds memory management capabilities to prevent resource exhaustion during long-running browser automation sessions.
🔍 Detailed Analysis ### Key Changes - **Configuration**: Added `BROWSER_MAX_PAGES_NUMBER` setting in `config.py` with a default value of 10 pages - **Page Management**: Modified `list_valid_pages()` method in `browser_factory.py` to accept a `max_pages` parameter and implement automatic page closing logic - **Logging**: Added warning logs when pages are automatically closed due to exceeding the limit, with a note about potential video recording impact ### Technical Implementation ```mermaid flowchart TD A[list_valid_pages called] --> B[Get all valid pages] B --> C{Pages count > max_pages?} C -->|No| D[Return all pages] C -->|Yes| E[Keep last max_pages pages] E --> F[Close oldest pages] F --> G[Log warning about closures] G --> H[Return reserved pages] ``` ### Impact - **Memory Management**: Prevents unlimited accumulation of browser pages that could lead to memory exhaustion - **Resource Control**: Provides configurable limits for different deployment scenarios and resource constraints - **Operational Visibility**: Warning logs help operators understand when automatic cleanup occurs and potential impacts on video recording functionality - **Backward Compatibility**: The change is non-breaking as it uses a default parameter value and maintains existing behavior when page count is within limits
_Created with [Palmier](https://www.palmier.io)_

body:
This streamlines the `COPY` into `$DEPENDABOT_HOME/` as a single command.

This reduces the layer count from two (or more) to only one.

This shouldn't have _that_ much impact on the cache hits since the two layers were adjacent. But it will reduce the calls to the docker registry since each layer is a separate call. And should make for slightly faster / trimmer builds when building from scratch.

author: shannonlee-dev
body:
## 요약
Student 모델 및 REST API 구현 완료 - SQLAlchemy 2.x ORM 모델, Pydantic v2 스키마, FastAPI CRUD 엔드포인트 포함

## 변경 사항

### 1. Student ORM 모델 구현 (app/models/student.py)
- SQLAlchemy 2.x 스타일 사용 (`Mapped`, `mapped_column`)
- UUID 기본 키 자동 생성 (`uuid.uuid4`)
- 필드: `id` (UUID), `name` (str), `birth` (date)
- IEPVersion과 1:N 관계 설정 (`cascade="all, delete-orphan"`)
- TYPE_CHECKING을 통한 순환 참조 방지

### 2. Student Pydantic 스키마 정의 (app/schemas/student.py)
- **StudentCreate**: 학생 생성 요청 스키마
  - name 필드: 1-100자 길이 검증
  - birth 필드: YYYY-MM-DD 형식 date 타입
- **StudentResponse**: 학생 응답 스키마
  - id, name, birth 포함
  - `ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)`로 ORM 모델 변환 지원

### 3. Student REST API 구현 (app/api/students.py)
- **POST /students**: 학생 생성
  - 요청: `{name: str, birth: date}`
  - 응답: `{id: UUID, name: str, birth: date}` (201 Created)
  - DB 트랜잭션 자동 관리 (commit, refresh)
- **GET /students**: 학생 목록 조회
  - Query 파라미터: `skip` (기본값 0), `limit` (기본값 100)
  - 응답: Student 배열
  - 페이지네이션 지원

### 4. 모델 등록 시스템 구성 (순환 참조 방지)
- **app/models/__init__.py**: 모든 모델 중앙 import
- **app/db/base.py**: Base 클래스만 정의 (모델 import 제거)
- **app/main.py**: `import app.models` 추가로 메타데이터 등록

### 5. 테스트 코드 추가 (tests/test_students.py)
- `test_import_student_model`: Student 모델 import 및 테이블명 검증
- `test_import_student_schemas`: 스키마 import 검증
- `test_import_student_router`: 라우터 prefix 및 tags 검증

## 테스트 방법

### 1. Student 모델 Import 검증
```bash
cd backend
python -c "from app.models.student import Student; print(f'Table: {Student.__tablename__}')"
```
**예상 출력:**
```
Table: student
```

### 2. Student 스키마 Import 검증
```bash
cd backend
python -c "from app.schemas.student import StudentCreate, StudentResponse; print('OK')"
```
**예상 출력:**
```
OK
```

### 3. Student Router 검증
```bash
cd backend
python -c "from app.api.students import router; print(f'Prefix: {router.prefix}'); print(f'Tags: {router.tags}')"
```
**예상 출력:**
```
Prefix: /students
Tags: ['Students']
```

### 4. FastAPI 앱 Import 검증
```bash
cd backend
python -c "from app.main import app; print(f'App title: {app.title}')"
```
**예상 출력:**
```
App title: IEP Planning Support Service
```

### 5. 전체 테스트 실행
```bash
cd backend
pytest tests/test_students.py -v
```
**예상 출력:**
```
tests/test_students.py::test_import_student_model PASSED                 [ 33%]
tests/test_students.py::test_import_student_schemas PASSED               [ 66%]
tests/test_students.py::test_import_student_router PASSED                [100%]

============================== 3 passed in 0.41s ===============================
```

### 6. Swagger UI에서 API 테스트 (해보세요)
```bash
# Docker Compose로 전체 스택 실행
docker compose up -d

# 브라우저에서 접속
# http://localhost:8000/docs
```

**Swagger UI에서 테스트:**
1. `POST /students` 엔드포인트 선택
2. Request body 입력:
   ```json
   {
     "name": "김철수",
     "birth": "2015-03-15"
   }
   ```
3. Execute 클릭 → 201 Created 응답 확인
4. `GET /students` 엔드포인트로 생성된 학생 조회

### 7. Docker 환경에서 검증
```bash
# DB 테이블 확인
docker compose exec db psql -U postgres -d iep_db -c "\dt"

# student 테이블 스키마 확인
docker compose exec db psql -U postgres -d iep_db -c "\d student"
```
**예상 출력:**
```
                  Table "public.student"
 Column |  Type   | Collation | Nullable | Default
--------+---------+-----------+----------+---------
 id     | uuid    |           | not null |
 name   | varchar |           | not null |
 birth  | date    |           | not null |
```

Closes #17

### What Changed
Added optional retry configuration parameters to the `dediregistry` plugin to improve reliability when communicating with DeDi registry services.

### Changes Made
- **Plugin Code**: Added `retry_max`, `retry_wait_min`, and `retry_wait_max` configuration fields to the dediregistry plugin, matching the implementation in the registry plugin
- **Tests**: Added test case to verify retry settings are correctly applied
- **Documentation**: Updated CONFIG.md and plugin README.md with retry parameter documentation

### Why This Change
The dediregistry plugin previously lacked retry logic. This change adds configurable exponential backoff retry behavior, making the plugin more resilient to transient failures.

Issue : https://github.com/Beckn-One/beckn-onix/issues/556

### Example Configuration
```yaml
registry:
  id: dediregistry
  config:

    registryName: "subscribers.beckn.one"

author: abhishek-singh591
body:
### Memory Optimization

Added periodic memory cleanup to FP16ClipTransform and SplitTensorsTransform to reduce memory usage during large tensor processing. Also avoids redundant external data loading when already present.

### Time Optimized ONNX Transform via Class Merging and Thread Pooling

It merges the FP16 and Split ONNX transform classes into a single implementation to eliminate redundant tensor loading and iteration. Additionally, the transform logic has been refactored to use a **thread pool**, replacing the previous sequential loop to parallelize tensor operations.

####  Performance Benchmarks:-

| Model           | Original Duration (s) | Optimized Duration (s) |
|----------------|------------------------|-------------------------|
| LLaMA 3.1 8B    | 88.35                  | 58.55                   |
| LLaMA 3.1 70B   | 1029.82                | 727.37                  |

> **Note:** Thread count is set to `os.cpu_count() * 4` to better handle I/O-bound workloads. Performance may vary depending on system hardware and threading capabilities.

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

body:
## Summary by Sourcery

Replace Notion-backed events endpoints with PostgreSQL-backed implementations and improve admin auth/database integration.

New Features:
- Expose events data from the PostgreSQL events table via /api/events and /api/events/:id endpoints returning structured JSON.
- Add a database healthCheck helper for use in health endpoints or monitoring.
- Introduce middleware to attach the authenticated user record to the request for downstream authorization checks.

Enhancements:
- Refine admin authorization by separating user attachment from admin role enforcement and improving error handling and logging.
- Standardize PostgreSQL connection setup using environment-based connection strings with production-aware SSL configuration.
- Tighten CSRF middleware integration to ensure the protection function is invoked correctly while still allowing specific API routes.

## Description

TypeScript compiler with `rootDir: "."` preserves source directory structure in `dist/`, but package.json referenced non-existent flat paths causing import failures. This PR fixes the path mismatches, bumps the package version, and updates documentation to use generic version references.

## Related Issue

Closes #58

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Test improvement

## Changes Made

Updated all package.json entry points to match actual compiled output structure:

- `main`: `./dist/index.js` → `./dist/src/index.js`
- `types`: `./dist/index.d.ts` → `./dist/src/index.d.ts`
- `bin.praxis`: `./dist/cli/index.js` → `./dist/src/cli/index.js`
- `exports["."]`: `./dist/index.*` → `./dist/src/index.*`
- `exports["./svelte"]`: `./dist/integrations/svelte.*` → `./dist/src/integrations/svelte.*`
- `exports["./schema"]`: `./dist/core/schema/types.*` → `./dist/core/schema-engine/types.*`
- `exports["./component"]`: `./dist/core/component/generator.*` → `./dist/ui/svelte-generator/index.*`
- `exports["./cloud"]`: `./dist/cloud/index.*` → `./dist/src/cloud/index.*`
- `exports["./components"]`: `./dist/components/index.d.ts` → `./dist/src/components/index.d.ts`
- `scripts.cli`: `node ./dist/cli/index.js` → `node ./dist/src/cli/index.js`

Version and documentation updates:

- Bumped package version from `1.0.0` to `1.0.1` (patch release for bug fix)
- Updated README.md to use "Latest" instead of hardcoded version numbers (`1.0.0` → `Latest`)
- Removed version numbers from section titles (e.g., "Protocol Versioning (v1.0.0)" → "Protocol Versioning")
- Updated PSF example to use `"$version": "latest"` instead of `"$version": "1.0.0"`

**Root cause**: tsconfig.json uses `rootDir: "."` which preserves directory structure when compiling to `dist/`, creating `dist/src/`, `dist/core/`, `dist/ui/` instead of a flat structure.

**Example** - imports now resolve correctly:
```javascript
import praxis from '@plures/praxis'           // → dist/src/index.js
import svelte from '@plures/praxis/svelte'   // → dist/src/integrations/svelte.js
import schema from '@plures/praxis/schema'   // → dist/core/schema-engine/types.js
import component from '@plures/praxis/component' // → dist/ui/svelte-generator/index.js
```

- [ ] New tests added for new functionality
- [x] Manual testing completed

npm run build
npm run typecheck
npm test
```

- All module exports load correctly (59 main, 8 svelte, 4 component, 31 cloud)
- CLI binary functional: `praxis --version` returns `1.0.1`

- [ ] Migration guide added/updated

None. Fixes broken functionality introduced by build structure mismatch.

- [ ] API documentation updated (if applicable)

body:
## Description [#32863](https://github.com/wazuh/wazuh/issues/32863) and [#32862](https://github.com/wazuh/wazuh/issues/32862) When building a policy that contains a circular reference between decoders, the engine can crash with a segmentation fault if one of the decoders in the cycle is also attached to a valid parent in the main graph. Minimal example: - A is the root decoder of the policy. - B declares A as a parent and also declares C as an additional parent. - C declares B as its parent. Graph: - A → B (valid path into the main graph) - B → C - C → B (cycle B ↔ C) Example decoders: ```yml --- name: decoder/testing/0 parse|event.original: - '' --- name: decoder/testing_c1/0 parents: - decoder/testing_c2/0 check: $tmp_json.custom_n >= 5 normalize: - map: - zz_tmp_custom_n: "Im testing_c1 5" --- name: decoder/testing_c2/0 parents: - decoder/testing/0 - decoder/testing_c1/0 check: $tmp_json.custom_n >= 10 normalize: - map: - zz_tmp_custom_n: "Im testing_c2 >= 10" ``` In this scenario: - `decoder/testing_c2/0` is part of the final execution graph because it is reachable from `decoder/testing/0`. - `decoder/testing_c1/0` and `decoder/testing_c2/0` form a cycle. - During policy build, the recursive traversal of the decoder graph falls into infinite recursion and ends with a segmentation fault. **Expected behavior**: Building a policy with circular references must never crash. Cycles should be detected and reported deterministically, and the policy build should fail with a clear error instead of ending in a segmentation fault. Additionally, decoders involved in a circular reference must not be silently omitted from the final graph; the policy build must reject the entire cyclic subgraph to avoid producing unreachable or “orphan” decoders and the resulting `Traceable not found `errors during testing. ## Proposed Changes - Introduced a reusable **cycle detection** routine for decoder graphs: - Added a `VisitState` enum (`NotVisited`, `Visiting`, `Visited`) and a [DFS-based detectCycle](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/detect-cycle-in-a-graph/) helper. - The helper keeps a stack of node names to reconstruct and log the full cycle path (e.g. `A -> B -> C -> A`). - Added a `validateAcyclic(const Graph&)` function in the policy factory: - Iterates over all nodes in the decoder subgraph. - Runs `detectCycle` from each non-visited node. - Logs and throws `std::runtime_error("Circular decoder reference detected: ...")` when a cycle is found. - Wired the validation into the policy build flow: - After building each decoder subgraph in `buildGraph`, the engine now calls `validateAcyclic(subgraph)` before building expressions. - This guarantees that any circular reference among decoders is rejected at build time, instead of reaching `buildSubgraphExpression` and causing a stack overflow / segfault. - Verified that: - Acyclic graphs with multi-parent decoders (e.g. E having parents D and B but no cycles) still build correctly. - The mixed case described in the issue (A root, B reachable from A and involved in B ↔ C) is now rejected with a clear “Circular decoder reference detected” error instead of crashing. ## Modified Files - `src/engine/source/builder/src/policy/factory.cpp` - `src/engine/source/builder/include/policy/factory.hpp` - `src/engine/source/builder/test/src/unit/policy/factory_test.cpp` ## Results and Evidence #### Unit Test - Self-loop ( `decoder/self/0 `): decoder lists itself as parent; ensures validator flags trivial cycles immediately. - Two-node cycle ( `decoder/a/0 ` ↔ `decoder/b/0 `): A references B, B references A; confirms mutual dependencies fail. - Three-node cycle ( `decoder/a/0 ` → `decoder/b/0 ` → `decoder/c/0 ` → `decoder/a/0 `): checks longer loops are traced and reported, matching the manual reproduction path. ```bash (venv) ╭─root@wazuh5x-dev /workspaces/Wazuh_5x/wazuh ‹bug/32863-decoder-cycle-segfault●› ╰─# ./src/build/engine/source/builder/builder_utest [----------] Global test environment tear-down [==========] 2867 tests from 57 test suites ran. (1110 ms total) [ PASSED ] 2864 tests. [ SKIPPED ] 3 tests, listed below: [ SKIPPED ] RevertedOrOperation/BuildSubgraphOrReverted.RevertedOrOperation/0 [ SKIPPED ] RevertedOrOperation/BuildSubgraphOrReverted.RevertedOrOperation/1 [ SKIPPED ] RevertedOrOperation/BuildSubgraphOrReverted.RevertedOrOperation/2 ``` ❗**NOTE:** The unit test shown in red fails locally due to a timeout, not because of this issue. It passes correctly in the workflow. #### Decoders
scenario 1 Issue Reproduction (Circular Reference B ↔ C) Minimal decoder set where B is reachable from the root (A), but also forms a direct cycle with C (B → C → B). This scenario reproduced the original segfault during policy build. **decoder** ```yml --- name: decoder/testing/0 parse|event.original: - '' --- name: decoder/testing_c1/0 parents: - decoder/testing_c2/0 check: $tmp_json.custom_n >= 5 normalize: - map: - zz_tmp_custom_n: "Im testing_c1 5" --- name: decoder/testing_c2/0 parents: - decoder/testing/0 - decoder/testing_c1/0 check: $tmp_json.custom_n >= 10 normalize: - map: - zz_tmp_custom_n: "Im testing_c2 >= 10" ``` ```bash (venv) ╭─root@wazuh5x-dev /workspaces/Wazuh_5x ╰─# engine-catalog -n system create decoder < intelligence-data/ruleset/decoders/decoder_testing.yml engine-catalog -n system create decoder < intelligence-data/ruleset/decoders/decoder_testing_c1.yml engine-catalog -n system create decoder < intelligence-data/ruleset/decoders/decoder_testing_c2.yml (venv) ╭─root@wazuh5x-dev /workspaces/Wazuh_5x ╰─# engine-policy create -p policy/testing-cycle/0 engine-policy asset-add -p policy/testing-cycle/0 -n system decoder/testing/0 engine-policy asset-add -p policy/testing-cycle/0 -n system decoder/testing_c1/0 engine-policy asset-add -p policy/testing-cycle/0 -n system decoder/testing_c2/0 ``` **Before** ```console ╭─root@wazuh5x-dev /workspaces/Wazuh_5x/wazuh/src/build/engine ‹bug/32863-decoder-cycle-segfault●› ╰─# ./wazuh-engine -f 2025/11/24 21:08:03 wazuh-analysisd: INFO: Router initialized. 2025/11/24 21:08:03 wazuh-analysisd: INFO: Archiver initialized. 2025/11/24 21:08:03 wazuh-analysisd: INFO: Content Manager Sync initialized. 2025/11/24 21:08:03 wazuh-analysisd: INFO: Initializing CTI Store ContentManager 2025/11/24 21:08:03 wazuh-analysisd: INFO: ContentManager: CTIStorageDB opened at '/var/ossec/engine/cti/assets_database' (open=true) 2025/11/24 21:08:03 wazuh-analysisd: INFO: CTI Store initialized 2025/11/24 21:08:03 wazuh-analysisd: WARNING: No environments found, deploying CTI content at startup. This may take a while... 2025/11/24 21:08:03 wazuh-analysisd: INFO: Starting Content Manager synchronization... 2025/11/24 21:08:03 wazuh-analysisd: WARNING: Could not deploy CTI content at startup: 'Failed to validate output 'output/indexer-security/0': Stage 'outputs' failed to build output 'wazuh-indexer': Indexer connector is not available' 2025/11/24 21:08:03 wazuh-analysisd: INFO: Starting CTI Store content synchronization 2025/11/24 21:08:03 wazuh-analysisd: INFO: Starting CTI Store ContentDownloader 2025/11/24 21:08:03 wazuh-analysisd: INFO: CTI Store ContentDownloader started successfully 2025/11/24 21:08:03 wazuh-analysisd: INFO: Server API_SRV started

body:
On AMD systems, `_check_intel_qsv()` incorrectly returns `True` because FFmpeg lists QSV encoders regardless of actual Intel hardware presence. This causes AMD Ryzen systems with Radeon graphics to be detected as "INTEL" with failing QSV encoders instead of "AMD" with working VAAPI encoders. ## Changes - **Added `_is_intel_gpu_present()` helper** — Verifies Intel GPU hardware exists before trusting FFmpeg's QSV encoder list. Uses three detection methods: - `vainfo` output for Intel driver strings - `lspci` for Intel VGA/Display controllers - `/sys/class/drm/card*/device/vendor` for Intel vendor ID (0x8086) - **Updated `_check_intel_qsv()`** — Now calls `_is_intel_gpu_present()` early and returns `False` if no Intel hardware found - **Added test coverage** — Tests for both AMD-detected-as-AMD and Intel-detected-as-Intel scenarios ## Result AMD Ryzen with Radeon 780M now correctly detects as: ``` type: "amd" decode_method: "vaapi" available_encoders: {h264: "h264_vaapi", hevc: "hevc_vaapi", av1: "av1_vaapi"} ``` Fixes #10

Implements a Python script to analyze betting model performance across spreads, totals, and moneylines from the trashduty/cbb repository's graded_results.csv.

## Implementation

**Core Analysis Sections (10 total)**
- Overall records for spreads (favorites/underdogs) and totals (overs/unders)
- Performance stratified by edge tiers: 0-1.9%, 2-2.9%, 3-3.9%, 4%+ for spreads, totals, and moneylines
- Spread performance by point spread ranges (0-4.5, 5-9.5, ..., 30+ points) for confident picks (probability > 0.5)
- Moneyline performance by win probability deciles (10-19%, 20-29%, ..., 90%+)
- All metrics calculated for both all games and consensus-flagged picks

**Data Handling**
- Fetches from GitHub API (commit `56448b2e`) with fallback to raw URL and local file
- Handles NaN values via `dropna()` on relevant columns before analysis
- Edge values in decimal format (0.025 = 2.5%)

**Output**
- Rich library tables with win-loss records and percentages
- Formatted section headers for readability

author: daniel-va
body:
Resolves #1278.
Part of #1587.

Fixes and cleans up any remaining code issues that are fallout from the large-scale layer refactoring. As one might have guessed, there were quite a lot.
Most commits should be quite self-contained and can be reviewed step-by-step - sorry for the massive PR.

**Features and Changes**  
- Migrate KML uploads to use the new layer infrastructure
- Add `Earthquakes` layer type (this one got lost on the way)
- Replace large parts of the old `MainStore` with services
- Remove unused code (mostly old layer stuff which has been refactored)
- Refactor translation file structure
- Add a way to reuse `order_of_properties` configs on 3dtiles
- Add `custom_properties` to layer config
- Add changes from `develop` (mostly OGC and 3dtiles v1.1)
- Improved handling of cesium render errors (there should be noticeably less of them now)
- Add documentation for new layer config and code
- Update DB to PSQL 16 (you might have to drop the db volume to get the db working again)

**Fixes**  
- Fix e2e tests
- Fix Ion Upload Modal in Catalog
- Fix display issues with Toolbox
- Fix selection of custom WMTS layers via search bar
- Fix picking on underground tiles
- Fix voxel layer rendering and removal causing render errors
- Fix disabled opacity configuration not working
- Fix picking on time travel layers requiring many non-parallelized requests
- Fix tooltips leaving unused elements in DOM after being removed

author: ariwk
body:
## Summary

- Fix `prCreation` from `"not-pending"` to `"status-success"` to properly support branch automerge (PRs only created after tests fail)
- Add `internalChecksFilter: "strict"` to enforce `minimumReleaseAge` stabilization period
- Add `dependencyDashboard: true` to monitor pending updates waiting for stabilization
- Reorder `packageRules` from least to most important (per Renovate docs)

## Background

The original config had a thinking error: `prCreation: "not-pending"` creates PRs even before tests complete, which defeats the "silent merge" purpose of branch automerge. The correct setting is `"status-success"` which only creates PRs when tests fail.

## Test plan

- [x] Validate JSON syntax with `jq empty default.json`
- [x] Verify pre-commit hooks pass
- [x] Test in downstream repository with Renovate bot

- **Built-in `map()` vs generator expression**: The `map()` function is implemented in C and operates directly on the iterables without creating intermediate tuples or executing Python bytecode for each iteration. The original code creates a generator expression that Python must iterate through, calling `function(a, b)` for each `zip(self.args, iterable)` pair, then wrapping it in `tuple()`.

**Performance impact:**
- The line profiler shows the critical line (tuple creation) dropped from 49.7% to just 0.7% of total execution time
- Overall speedup of 12% with particularly strong gains for positional arguments cases
- Test results show 20-55% speedup for `args` cases, while `kwargs` cases (unchanged) show minimal gains

**Why this works:**
- `map(function, self.args, iterable)` directly applies `function` to corresponding elements without Python-level iteration overhead
- Eliminates the intermediate generator object creation and tuple conversion
- The `*` unpacking works identically with both approaches, maintaining exact same behavior

**Workload benefits:**
- Most effective for cases with positional arguments (which trigger the optimized path)
- Larger argument lists show greater relative improvements (up to 55% in large-scale tests)
- No performance regression for keyword arguments path, which remains unchanged

## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

body:
## Summary

Implements a production-ready plugin system for CLI commands with thread-safe registry, security validation, and comprehensive documentation.

Resolves #1692

## Implementation Overview

### Core Components (7 modules)

1. **base.py** - Abstract PluginBase class and exception hierarchy
2. **registry.py** - Thread-safe singleton with double-checked locking
3. **decorator.py** - @register_plugin decorator for automatic registration
4. **discovery.py** - Secure plugin discovery with validation
5. **loader.py** - Plugin loading with optional caching
6. **builtin/hello.py** - Working example plugin
7. **__init__.py** - Public API via __all__

### Security Features

- **Path Traversal Prevention**: Validates plugin directory paths
- **File Size Limits**: Default 1MB per plugin file
- **Permission Checks**: Verifies read permissions
- **Resilient Processing**: One plugin failure doesn't stop discovery
- **Input Validation**: Comprehensive PluginBase validation

### Architecture

- **SOLID Principles**: Single responsibility, open/closed, interface segregation
- **Thread Safety**: Double-checked locking for singleton
- **Stateless Plugins**: New instance per load by default
- **Optional Caching**: Module-level caching for performance
- **Standard Library Only**: No external dependencies
- **Bricks & Studs Pattern**: Self-contained modules with clear public APIs

## Test Results

### Unit Tests (34 tests)
✅ All passing - 60% of testing pyramid
- PluginBase tests (5)
- PluginRegistry tests (8)
- Decorator tests (5)
- Discovery tests (7)
- Loading tests (9)

### Integration Tests (14 tests)
✅ All passing - 30% of testing pyramid
- Complete workflow (5)
- Multiple plugins (3)
- Error handling (3)
- Thread safety (3)

### Local End-to-End Testing (8 scenarios)
✅ All passing - verified user workflows
- Custom plugin creation
- Plugin loading and execution
- Stateless behavior
- Caching mechanism
- Error handling
- Multiple argument types
- Directory discovery
- Invalid plugin handling

**Total: 48/48 tests passing (100%)**

## Philosophy Compliance

Reviewer agent score: **9.4/10**

✅ **Ruthless Simplicity**: Standard library only, minimal abstractions
✅ **Modular Design**: Clear module boundaries with defined contracts
✅ **Zero-BS Implementation**: No stubs, TODOs, or fake implementations
✅ **SOLID Principles**: Applied throughout
✅ **Bricks & Studs**: Self-contained modules, regeneratable from specs

## Documentation

Created comprehensive documentation following Diataxis framework:

1. **Reference**: docs/reference/plugin-api.md (738 lines)
   - Complete API documentation
   - All methods, parameters, return values
   - Working code examples

2. **Tutorial**: docs/tutorials/create-your-first-plugin.md (350 lines)
   - 6-step beginner guide (15 minutes)
   - From zero to working plugin
   - Common issues and solutions

3. **How-to**: docs/howto/troubleshoot-plugins.md (657 lines)
   - Diagnostic table for quick issue identification
   - 6 problem categories with solutions
   - Debugging strategies

4. **Explanation**: src/amplihack/plugins/README.md (730 lines)
   - Architecture overview
   - Lifecycle documentation
   - Security considerations
   - Testing strategies

## Public API

Exported via `__all__`:
- `PluginBase` - Abstract base class
- `PluginRegistry` - Singleton registry
- `register_plugin` - Decorator
- `discover_plugins` - Discovery function
- `load_plugin` - Loading function
- `load_all_plugins` - Batch loading
- Exception classes: `PluginError`, `PluginValidationError`, `PluginNotFoundError`, `PluginLoadError`

## Example Usage

```python
from amplihack.plugins import PluginBase, register_plugin

@register_plugin(name="hello", description="Prints hello message")
class HelloPlugin(PluginBase):
    def execute(self, args):
        name = args.get("name", "Friend")
        print(f"Hello, {name}!")
        return f"Hello, {name}!"
```

## Breaking Changes

None - this is a new feature addition with no impact on existing code.

- [x] Thread-safe implementation

author: szetszwo
body:
## What changes were proposed in this pull request?

In HDDS-13974, the client sends a single stream read block request and the datanode will reply the entire block in multiple responses. However, the client may read only a part of the block or read slowly. In such cases, the datanode will queue up all the block data in the gRPC layer.

In this PR, we
- add required length L to the request and then the datanode only replies L bytes of data;
- support multiple checksums in a single response;
- support pre-read;
- change the datanode to open and close the block file only once per gRPC stream.

## What is the link to the Apache JIRA

HDDS-13975

## How was this patch tested?

Adding new tests.

author: janpaepke
body:
## Summary

Adds support for the OAuth API endpoints, enabling applications to generate and revoke OAuth tokens programmatically.

## Changes

- **Added OAuth data model** in `src/data/oauth/` with Token response type and enums (GrantType, TokenType)
- **Implemented `OAuthBinder`** with `create()` for token generation and `revoke()` for token revocation
- **Added `rawRequest` to NetworkClient** as an escape hatch for endpoints that don't follow standard v2 conventions (OAuth uses Basic Auth, form-urlencoded body, and `/oauth2/tokens` endpoint)
- **Exported OAuth types** in `types.ts` and enums in `createMollieClient.ts`
- **Added unit tests** verifying request format (Basic Auth header, form-urlencoded body, discriminated union grant types)

The implementation uses discriminated unions on `grant_type` for type-safe token generation (authorization_code vs refresh_token grants).

## API Details

The OAuth API provides:
- Token generation via authorization code exchange
- Token generation via refresh token
- Token revocation for both access and refresh tokens

## Note

Unable to add integration tests as this endpoint requires OAuth application credentials. Unit tests verify the request format but cannot verify actual API behavior.

**This will be released as a beta first.**

## References

- Closes #456
- [OAuth API docs](https://docs.mollie.com/reference/oauth-api)
- [Generate tokens](https://docs.mollie.com/reference/oauth-generate-tokens)
- [Revoke token](https://docs.mollie.com/reference/oauth-revoke-token)

author: json-andriopoulos
body:
## Describe changes

This story extends the existing step-heartbeat logic by:

- Letting users set a maximum “heartbeat_healthy_threshold” for heartbeat-enabled steps before they’re deemed unhealthy (system-gated).
- Adding evaluation of step health from heartbeat signals.
- Using that health check to preemptively stop unhealthy step execution in the Kubernetes orchestrator.
- Using that health check to invalidate pipeline tokens when a pipeline enters an unhealthy state.
- Ensuring all orchestrators can gracefully stop running heartbeat-enabled steps when a pipeline is stopped.

body:
I transformed the original NeoForge project into a multiloader project (NeoForge + Fabric) using Architectury.

I couldn't possibly have made this a smaller PR (sorry about that), so I'll try to document all the changes I made:

### Bug fixes

I have introduced the following bug fixes (I also have made other PRs including these, merging them first would probably be good to have them as separate commits):
* Barrel Golem sound keyframe warning
* Default size for Slime Golem
* Golem target selection

### Multiplatform changes

* Architectury multiloader template used as base for project structure
* Block render type registration in `GolemOverhaulClient` (for cutout blocks on Fabric)
* Entity renderers registered via Architectury in `GolemOverhaulClient`
* Key mappings registered via Architectury in `GolemOverhaulClient`
* Replaced `IShearable` interface from NeoForge with own implementation that is handled exactly like NeoForge's but with an Architectury event (`IShearable`, `ModEvents#registerShearInteractions`)
* Replaced NeoForge events with Architectury ones in `ModEvents` (and `GolemOverhaulClient` for handling key mappings)
* Platform-dependent implementations for adding spawn eggs in `ModItems`
* Architectury registries used in `ModEntityTypes`
* Entrypoints for JEI/REI plugins in `fabric.mod.json`
* REI plugin class `GolemOverhaulReiPluginNeoForge` for NeoForge (necessary annotation is not available in common)

### NeoForge `biome_modifier` data

I removed these datapack json files, as they are now handled in a multi-platform way in `ModEntityTypes#registerBiomeModifications`.

### Datagen

I moved all datagen classes into the neoforge module and made it output to the common module. \
I don't have much experience with datagen, so I hope this is a good way to handle it in an Architectury project, but it definitely works and I made sure to exclude the .cache folder from resource processing in the common module. \
I also now excluded the datagen classes from the neoforge build output.

### Release workflow

I've updated the pipeline to respect the new output directories and also upload the Fabric release. \
I've also removed a bit of metadata parameters, as those are now being read from the `neoforge.mods.toml`/`fabric.mod.json` files contained in the compiled jars (including the dependencies with correct slugs for modrinth/curseforge). \
I've already confirmed this to work perfectly in a little mc-publish test environment.

### Maven publishing

This is something I never did myself, so hope I didn't do anything wrong here, please have a look at this in `build.gradle`.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #146 - Archived specs now display content correctly in the dashboard.

## Problem

When viewing archived specifications in the dashboard, the content viewer displayed "No content available" for all documents (requirements, design, tasks), even though the files exist and contain data.

## Root Cause

The frontend was calling `/api/projects/:projectId/specs/:name/all/archived` for archived specs, but this endpoint did not exist in the backend. The existing `/all` endpoint only reads from the active specs path (`.spec-workflow/specs/{name}/`).

## Solution

Added a new API endpoint `/api/projects/:projectId/specs/:name/all/archived` that reads documents from the archive path (`.spec-workflow/archive/specs/{name}/`) instead of the active specs path.

## Testing

1. Archive a spec with completed documents
2. Navigate to Dashboard → Specs → Archive tab
3. Click on the archived spec
4. Verify all documents (requirements, design, tasks) display their content correctly

author: vincetyy
body:
This pull request migrates the YouTube upload functionality in the `creation_service` from using service account authentication to using OAuth with a refresh token, making it compatible with YouTube's requirements for channel uploads. It also introduces new helper scripts to automate credential setup and testing, and updates the documentation and codebase to reflect these changes.

**YouTube OAuth Migration**

* Replaced service account authentication with OAuth: The uploader now reads `YOUTUBE_CLIENT_ID`, `YOUTUBE_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `YOUTUBE_REFRESH_TOKEN` from environment variables, and uses them to authenticate uploads via OAuth instead of a service account JSON. (`creation_service/app/services/uploader.go`, `creation_service/app/services/processor.go`, `creation_service/main.go`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8d13b6629a93e29c2782216d724c65d93cc992a67c215beaf089045f138b60c3L20-R74) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-63ee744e1906976884e40d9ceaab5b9e27885355178a8881c3cd53fb8051182dL24-R25) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a2e9d37885bcb97a596f3d857d60c83a6787bdd45090d7287242b9dd71a08424L31-R28)
* Updated error handling and documentation to reflect OAuth usage, including new troubleshooting steps and Docker instructions. (`creation_service/README.md`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-316c1d8a9312fbf93bcb876df20235a61bf60d16c45c99358b95ff2f13f480a3L75-R75) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-316c1d8a9312fbf93bcb876df20235a61bf60d16c45c99358b95ff2f13f480a3L98-R145) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-316c1d8a9312fbf93bcb876df20235a61bf60d16c45c99358b95ff2f13f480a3L261-R301) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-316c1d8a9312fbf93bcb876df20235a61bf60d16c45c99358b95ff2f13f480a3L306-R351)

**Credential Setup and Helper Scripts**

* Added `scripts/get_refresh_token.py` to generate a refresh token via the OAuth consent flow, and output credentials as JSON and shell environment variables.
* Added `scripts/setup_creation_service_credentials.sh` to automate credential setup, token caching, and environment variable management for the service.
* Updated `.gitignore` to protect secret files and credential caches. (`creation_service/.gitignore`)

**Testing and CLI Improvements**

* Added `cmd/upload/main.go`, a CLI tool for uploading a video to YouTube with metadata, using the OAuth credentials.
* Added `scripts/test_upload.sh`, a shell script to smoke-test the upload process, including credential setup and environment sourcing.

These changes modernize the authentication flow, make the service easier to set up for new users, and enable robust local and automated testing of the YouTube upload functionality.

body:
This pull request introduces several important updates to the Novagate API key gateway, focusing on licensing, documentation, middleware enhancements, and package configuration. The most significant changes include the addition of an MIT license, major improvements to the documentation, the introduction of a new suspension middleware for abusive API keys, and updates to the example and main export files for better usability and clarity.

**Licensing and Documentation Updates**
* Added an explicit MIT license to the repository for open-source clarity and legal compliance.
* Revamped the `README.md` with clearer feature descriptions, installation instructions, and improved formatting for easier onboarding.

**Middleware and Example Enhancements**
* Introduced a new `createSuspensionMiddleware` in `src/security/suspension.js` to automatically suspend API keys exceeding abuse thresholds, and integrated this into the HTTP example workflow. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e0f1749a64c59715bb13db6ffd6dfcc2672ca6128c51da9e2236b54b49e0e293R1-R31) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-641bf590c341ea107542be5005c10e73eee7d6fd999ae8da2003fac9813c8700R98-R124)
* Updated example code organization: renamed `example/http.js` to `examples/http.js`, refactored imports to use the new `src/` structure, and added a `suspended` property to user objects for suspension tracking. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-641bf590c341ea107542be5005c10e73eee7d6fd999ae8da2003fac9813c8700L2-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-641bf590c341ea107542be5005c10e73eee7d6fd999ae8da2003fac9813c8700R37) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-641bf590c341ea107542be5005c10e73eee7d6fd999ae8da2003fac9813c8700R46)

**Package Configuration and Exports**
* Updated `package.json` to point to the new entry file (`src/index.js`), switched license to MIT, added keywords, and included repository metadata for improved discoverability and compliance.
* Created a central export file `src/index.js` to cleanly expose all core middleware and utility functions for easier integration.

These changes collectively improve the project’s usability, maintainability, and legal clarity, while adding robust protection against abusive API key usage.

## Merge first

- [x] https://github.com/getkirby/kirby/pull/7696

## Changelog 
<!--
Add relevant release notes. Keep the target audience (Kirby user) in mind.
Reference issues from the `kirby` repo  or ideas from `feedback.getkirby.com`.
-->

### ♻️ Refactored

- New `Kirby\Form\Field\OptionField` abstract class
- New `Kirby\Form\Field\RadioField` class
- New `Kirby\Form\Mixin\Options` mixin
- New `Kirby\Form\Mixin\Columns` mixin

### 🚨 Breaking changes

- The radio field does no longer remove invalid values on submit or fill, but uses the option validator to warn if a value is invalid. This is more in line with what other input fields do in Kirby and has massive performance benefits. It also means that you can deliberately store a non-existing option if you skip validation, which also might be useful in some cases.
- The `api` and `query` options for the radio and other option classes are no longer available. Queries and API calls to fetch options have now to be declared directly in the options property. 
```yaml
fields: 
  myRadio: 
    type: radio
    options: 
      type: query
      query: some.query
```

or 

```yaml
fields: 
  myRadio: 
    type: radio
    options: 
      type: api
      url: /some/options/api
```

If you need to cancel that sign-off, type `#hold-off` instead. *Signing off means the document can be published at any time.* Note, this is a formatting and standards review, not a technical review.

## Merge and publish
- After you `#sign-off`, there is a separate PR Review team that will review the PR and describe any necessary feedback before merging.

https://issues.redhat.com/browse/AROSLSRE-265

### What

Adds a different deletion workflow to the e2e expired resource groups cleanup command to allow deletion of e2e leftover resources in personal dev envs. It requires a different workflow because the RP is already gone when the cleanup is run, so the only thing that can be done is: 
* check for expired RGs as usual
* delete first the corresponding `*--managed` RGs
* delete the RGs

An additional location filter was added because both personal dev env e2e runs and production e2e runs share the same subscription, but run using different locations.

We have leftover resources from personal dev env e2e runs that run as PR pre-submits
